entries.title: Virtual iPhone Studio
entries.summary: An interactive silver iPhone concept with a rotatable 3D model and a working screen. Explore apps, calculate, save notes, change wallpapers, and switch into screen-only mode.
notes: Day 1 delivers the hardware and interaction milestone: orbit, zoom, front/back views, side controls, lock/unlock, and a live HTML screen on the 3D model.
Calculator, local notes, wallpapers, display settings, and synthesized audio work without an API key. Weather, camera, phone, and messages are labeled simulations.
Production build and desktop/mobile browser checks passed. AI integration is planned for a later milestone.

entries.title: ROMPOD — Rawmware Audio System
entries.summary: A Winamp-inspired audio workstation with movable metallic panels, three immersive visualizers, eight skins, YouTube playlists and local audio with a real ten-band equalizer.
notes: Evolves the Pocket Amp beta into a full-screen Rawmware music environment. Day 2 is September 29; this milestone was published September 30, 2026.
Desktop and mobile browser checks passed on the public player, including local audio playback, seeking, source switching, analyser output, equalizer controls, skins and window interactions.

The supplied YouTube playlist returned an embedding restriction during verification. Local audio playback is verified; YouTube availability depends on each playlist and video. YouTube visuals are generative; local audio drives real analysis.

entries.title: AIctually Help — practical AI for everyday life
entries.summary: Ready-to-use prompts right on the page, with a bigger idea: teach people practical AI skills through nonprofits, starting with everyday needs like email.
notes: The idea is to give people something they can try immediately: copy a prompt, paste it into an AI app, and use it for a real task.
Start with the basics, including setting up email and learning how to ask for help. The longer-term idea is to teach people at nonprofits how I use AI.
Day 3 is September 30, 2026. This archive entry and its blog post were added October 2, 2026. Nonprofit workshops are an idea to pursue, not a completed program.

entries.title: Cyber Castle — Security Automations
entries.summary: Ten open-source security automations are presented as interactive browser simulations, with kid-friendly and technical explanations of what each helper does.
notes: Cyber Castle turns ten security projects by ChiefGyk3D into safe, in-browser simulations that visitors can explore without scanning or connecting to real systems.
The page includes kid-friendly and grown-up modes, an interactive castle map, individual helper demos, optional sound effects, and clear links to the original open-source projects.
The reviewed static build is hosted on RawmWare so selecting Day 4 opens the application directly; project notes and source remain secondary links.

entries.title: github.fetch — Open Source, Ready to Run
entries.summary: A live discovery feed that turns fresh open-source repositories into plain-English browser launch guides, local commands, licensing context, and make-it-yours prompts.
notes: The application reads the public github.fetch feed and lets visitors search, filter, sort, open, fork, and copy setup guidance for newly discovered repositories.

A GitHub Actions pulse runs every 15 minutes and paces authored scout commits toward a floor of 60 per UTC day; the interface verifies today's default-branch scout commits through GitHub's public API.
The frontend is portable static HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in the github.fetch repository, so it can move from the Day 5 route to a standalone domain later.
